title: Sentence Structures Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the four main sentence structures and what each one does.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language sentence structures walkthrough — simple, compound, complex, compound-complex.
final_note: You learned the four main sentence types and how to identify each in any text.

concepts.def: One independent clause — one main idea
Main clause + at least one subordinate clause
Two main clauses + a subordinate clause
A clause that can stand alone as a sentence
A clause that can't stand alone

walkthroughs.body_html:
A simple sentence has one independent clause: 'She ran.'

Punchy. Direct. Hits hard.

Compound: two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so).

'She ran AND she did not look back.'

Complex: one main + one subordinate.

'Although she was exhausted, she ran.'

The subordinate clause adds nuance.

mcqs.q: 'She ran, and she did not look back' is a:
options: Simple sentence
Compound sentence
Complex sentence
Minor sentence
Birds sing.
Birds sing and squirrels chatter.
Although it was raining, birds sang.
Sing!
A noun is always a person, place or thing.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
Standard English is the same as Received Pronunciation.
By the word's grammatical function in a sentence — not its meaning. The same word can belong to different classes depending on use (e.g. 'run' as noun or verb).
Standard English is the same as Received Pronunciation.
Standard English is the original and correct form of the language.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
A dialect that has gained social and institutional prestige — used in education and formal writing; it is one variety, not inherently superior in linguistic terms.

mcqs.q: How does Piaget's theory relate language to cognitive development?
options: Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.

Language develops as a consequence of cognitive development — children must first develop concepts (object permanence, conservation) before they can express them linguistically. Cognition leads language.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
Piaget said language drives cognitive development.
